chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from one of our companions, who said:

A group of people came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and found a son of his who was sick. They saw concern and grief in him, and he would not remain at rest. He said, 'By Allah, if anything happens to him, we fear that we will see from him what we dislike.'

He said, 'They did not wait long before they heard the outcry upon him. Behold, he had come out to them with a cheerful face, in a state different from what he had been in before. They said to him, 'May Allah sacrifice us for you! We were afraid that, from what we saw of you, if it were to happen, we would see from you what would sadden us.'
So he said to them, 'We love to be healthy regarding those we love. But when the Command of Allah comes, we submit regarding what we love.'
ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Baqir demonstrate patience and submission to divine decree upon the death of his son?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia concept of 'naturalness' (tabi'iyyah) in the Imams, demonstrating that their emotional responses to loss are genuine human reactions rather than mere pretense, yet they are immediately followed by conscious spiritual submission. It contextualizes the recitation of 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un' not just as a ritual, but as a profound psychological transition from personal attachment to divine acceptance, reinforcing the theological balance between feeling and faith.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from one of our companions who said,

‘A group of people came over to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, so they found a son of his<sup>asws</sup> to be sick, and they saw from him<sup>asws</sup> worries, and gloom, and not being at rest. So they said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! If something happens to him we are afraid that we would see from him<sup>asws</sup> what we do not like’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘It was not long before we heard the shrieking upon him, and he<sup>asws</sup> had come out with a glad face in a changed state which was upon him<sup>asws</sup> beforehand. So they said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May we be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! We were afraid from what we would see from you<sup>asws</sup> if (death) were to occur that we would see from you<sup>asws</sup> what would make us gloomy’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said to them: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> love that we<sup>asws</sup> have good health regarding the ones we<sup>asws</sup> love. But when the Command of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> comes, we<sup>asws</sup> submit with regards to what we<sup>asws</sup> love’.
en.sarwar: 14. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from certain persons of our people who have said the following:

“Once a group of people came to visit abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, to find out how one of his children suffering from illness was doing. They found him deeply concerned, grieved and restless. The narrator has said that they said, ‘By Allah, if something happens to him (the child), we are afraid we will see something from him (the Imam) that we will not like to see.’

The narrator has said that within a short time they began to hear weeping and crying for him. On the other hand, the Imam came to them, relaxed, free of concerns and totally changed from his previous conditions. They said, ‘May Allah keep our souls in the service of your cause, from seeing your condition we were afraid that if something happens, we may see things that will cause us a great deal of sorrow.’
The Imam then said to them, ‘We love to enjoy the wellbeing of whatever we love, but when the command of Allah comes we submit ourselves to what He loves.’”
